programme.title: VPC, Private Connectivity and Hybrid Networking Follow Along
programme.topic: Amazon VPC, Private Connectivity and Hybrid Networking
programme.outcome: Build a two-AZ VPC with public, private and isolated subnet tiers; configure route tables, security groups, a network ACL, a public NAT gateway, S3 gateway and SSM interface VPC endpoints; connect a second VPC first with peering and then Transit Gateway; design PrivateLink, Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect architectures; enable VPC Flow Logs; and safely remove only the resources created by the lab.
programme.statusNotice: Offline authoring manuscript only — not locally validated, imported, accepted, approved, published or fingerprinted.
completionDefinition: fa-vpc-core contains public, private and isolated subnet tiers across eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.
Only public subnets route directly to the internet gateway; private subnets use fa-vpc-nat-a; isolated subnets have no default internet route.
Stateful security groups and a stateless isolated-subnet NACL are configured and compared.
An S3 gateway endpoint modifies selected route tables while an SSM interface endpoint creates private ENIs in isolated subnets.
fa-vpc-peer is first connected through direct VPC peering, then that path is replaced by Transit Gateway routing.
Complete PrivateLink, Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect architecture plans are produced without creating unnecessary NLB/VPN/Direct Connect costs.
VPC Flow Logs are Active and target the private account-derived S3 bucket.
All chargeable NAT, interface-endpoint and Transit Gateway resources are deleted before the temporary IAM identity and local files.

tasks.title: Verify account, Region and networking scope
tasks.goal: Confirm a clean training account, AWS CLI and eu-west-2 before any resource exists.
tasks.whyItMatters: Known identity and Region reduce false troubleshooting signals.
tasks.examRelevance: Networking questions combine routing, isolation, endpoints and hybrid patterns.

browserSteps.instruction: Sign in to the disposable AWS training account.
Confirm no resource beginning fa-vpc already exists.
Open Windows PowerShell and run aws --version.
Confirm the console Region is Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Do not create or use root access keys; root is used only for Task 2 bootstrap and Task 18 final IAM-user deletion.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - verify CLI
cliBlocks.content: aws --version

cliBlocks.title: Bash - verify CLI
cliBlocks.content: aws --version

expectedResults: AWS CLI prints a version.
No fa-vpc resource exists.

verificationChecks.text: The CLI works.
The console Region is eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Create the temporary VPC networking IAM user
tasks.goal: Use root only to create fa-vpc-admin, one temporary access key and the complete lab policy.
tasks.whyItMatters: The lab needs controlled rights for VPC, NAT, endpoints, peering, TGW, Flow Logs and one S3 bucket.
tasks.examRelevance: Least-privilege still matters in networking labs.

browserSteps.instruction: Sign in as root only for this bootstrap task.
Open IAM > Users > Create user.
User name: fa-vpc-admin; enable console access.
Create the user.
Open IAM > Policies > Create policy > JSON.
Paste the complete fa-vpc-admin-policy block below.
Create policy fa-vpc-admin-policy and attach it directly to fa-vpc-admin.
Open Security credentials and create exactly one access key for CLI use.
Copy the access key only to a temporary secure location.
Sign out of root and sign in as fa-vpc-admin.

cliBlocks.title: No root CLI command
cliBlocks.content: # Complete this one-time bootstrap in the IAM console. Do not create root access keys.

expectedResults: fa-vpc-admin exists.
fa-vpc-admin-policy is attached.
Root is signed out.

verificationChecks.text: The current browser session is fa-vpc-admin.
AdministratorAccess is not attached.

tasks.title: Configure the CLI profile and create architecture files
tasks.goal: Configure fa-vpc-admin and save the exact core, PrivateLink and hybrid network designs.
tasks.whyItMatters: The design files keep CIDRs and non-deployed expensive services explicit.
tasks.examRelevance: Intermediate network design should start with CIDR/routing intent.

Run aws configure --profile fa-vpc-admin.
Enter the temporary key only in protected prompts; set Region eu-west-2 and output json.
Run get-caller-identity.

Create network-design.json, privatelink-plan.json and hybrid-connectivity-plan.json.
Paste the complete blocks below and verify the 10.80.0.0/16 and 10.90.0.0/16 CIDRs do not overlap.

tasks.title: Create fa-vpc-core and six subnet tiers
tasks.goal: Create public, private and isolated subnets across eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.
tasks.whyItMatters: Equivalent subnet tiers across AZs make resilience and routing boundaries visible.
tasks.examRelevance: Subnet purpose is ultimately determined by routes and addressing, not the subnet name.

browserSteps.instruction: Open VPC in eu-west-2 and create VPC only named fa-vpc-core with CIDR 10.80.0.0/16.
Enable DNS hostnames on fa-vpc-core.
Create fa-vpc-public-a in eu-west-2a: 10.80.0.0/24.
Create fa-vpc-public-b in eu-west-2b: 10.80.1.0/24.
Create fa-vpc-private-a in eu-west-2a: 10.80.10.0/24.
Create fa-vpc-private-b in eu-west-2b: 10.80.11.0/24.
Create fa-vpc-isolated-a in eu-west-2a: 10.80.20.0/24.
Create fa-vpc-isolated-b in eu-west-2b: 10.80.21.0/24.
Do not enable public IPv4 auto-assignment on private or isolated subnets.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create core VPC
cliBlocks.content: $CORE_VPC_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-core}]" --query Vpc.VpcId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - DNS hostnames
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --enable-dns-hostnames "{\"Value\":true}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create six subnets
cliBlocks.content:
$PUBLIC_A_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.80.0.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-public-a}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PUBLIC_B_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.80.1.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-public-b}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PRIVATE_A_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.80.10.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-private-a}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PRIVATE_B_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.80.11.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-private-b}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$ISOLATED_A_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.80.20.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-isolated-a}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$ISOLATED_B_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.80.21.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-isolated-b}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: fa-vpc-core has six /24 subnets across two AZs.
Private/isolated subnets do not auto-assign public IPv4.

verificationChecks.text: All CIDRs match network-design.json.
Three subnet tiers exist in each AZ.

tasks.title: Create tier-specific route tables and internet gateway
tasks.goal: Give only public subnets an IGW default route and give each private/isolated subnet an explicit route-table association.
tasks.whyItMatters: Routing is what makes a subnet public, private or isolated.
tasks.examRelevance: Route destination/target matching is a core SAA-C03 networking skill.

browserSteps.instruction: Create internet gateway fa-vpc-igw and attach it to fa-vpc-core.
Create fa-vpc-public-rt, fa-vpc-private-a-rt, fa-vpc-private-b-rt, fa-vpc-isolated-a-rt and fa-vpc-isolated-b-rt.
Add 0.0.0.0/0 -> fa-vpc-igw only to fa-vpc-public-rt.
Associate both public subnets with fa-vpc-public-rt.
Associate each private subnet with its matching private route table.
Associate each isolated subnet with its matching isolated route table.
Verify neither isolated route table contains 0.0.0.0/0.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - IGW
cliBlocks.content:
$IGW_ID = aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications "ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-igw}]" --query InternetGateway.InternetGatewayId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id $IGW_ID --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create route tables
cliBlocks.content:
$PUBLIC_RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-public-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PRIVATE_A_RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-private-a-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PRIVATE_B_RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-private-b-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$ISOLATED_A_RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-isolated-a-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$ISOLATED_B_RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-isolated-b-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - route/associate
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PUBLIC_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id $IGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $PUBLIC_RT_ID --subnet-id $PUBLIC_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $PUBLIC_RT_ID --subnet-id $PUBLIC_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --subnet-id $PRIVATE_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --subnet-id $PRIVATE_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $ISOLATED_A_RT_ID --subnet-id $ISOLATED_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $ISOLATED_B_RT_ID --subnet-id $ISOLATED_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: Only fa-vpc-public-rt has the IGW default route.
Every non-public subnet has an explicit route-table association.

verificationChecks.text: Both isolated route tables lack 0.0.0.0/0.
Public route target is fa-vpc-igw.

tasks.title: Create a public NAT gateway and private egress routes
tasks.goal: Create fa-vpc-nat-a in public-a and route both private subnets to it.
tasks.whyItMatters: NAT provides outbound IPv4 egress while private subnets avoid direct IGW routing.
tasks.examRelevance: NAT is egress, not transitive inter-VPC routing.
warnings: NAT Gateway and Elastic IP incur charges while present.

browserSteps.instruction: Allocate Elastic IP fa-vpc-nat-eip.
Create public NAT gateway fa-vpc-nat-a in fa-vpc-public-a using that EIP.
Wait for Available.
Add 0.0.0.0/0 -> fa-vpc-nat-a to fa-vpc-private-a-rt and fa-vpc-private-b-rt.
Do not add a NAT route to isolated route tables.
Record the training compromise: private-b depends on a zonal NAT in eu-west-2a; production designs should address cross-AZ/failure requirements.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - EIP/NAT
cliBlocks.content:
$EIP_ALLOC_ID = aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc --tag-specifications "ResourceType=elastic-ip,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-nat-eip}]" --query AllocationId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$NAT_ID = aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id $PUBLIC_A_ID --allocation-id $EIP_ALLOC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=natgateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-nat-a}]" --query NatGateway.NatGatewayId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 wait nat-gateway-available --nat-gateway-ids $NAT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - private NAT routes
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id $NAT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id $NAT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: NAT is Available.
Both private RTs use NAT for 0.0.0.0/0.
Isolated RTs remain without default routes.

verificationChecks.text: NAT is in public-a and has the EIP.
No isolated route targets NAT.

tasks.title: Create endpoint security groups and an isolated-subnet NACL
tasks.goal: Create SG reference rules and a stateless NACL for isolated subnets.
tasks.whyItMatters: SGs are stateful ENI controls; NACLs are stateless subnet controls.
tasks.examRelevance: Stateful versus stateless is a frequent exam distinction.

browserSteps.instruction: Create fa-vpc-client-sg in fa-vpc-core with no inbound rules.
Create fa-vpc-endpoint-sg in fa-vpc-core.
Allow inbound TCP 443 to fa-vpc-endpoint-sg only from fa-vpc-client-sg.
Create fa-vpc-isolated-nacl.
Add inbound rule 100 Allow ALL from 10.80.0.0/16.
Add outbound rule 100 Allow ALL to 10.80.0.0/16.
Leave implicit deny for other traffic.
Associate both isolated subnets with fa-vpc-isolated-nacl.
Explain that the symmetric NACL rules are needed because NACLs are stateless.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - SGs
cliBlocks.content:
$CLIENT_SG_ID = aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-vpc-client-sg --description "Training clients" --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$ENDPOINT_SG_ID = aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-vpc-endpoint-sg --description "Endpoint HTTPS" --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $ENDPOINT_SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 443 --source-group $CLIENT_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - NACL
cliBlocks.content:
$NACL_ID = aws ec2 create-network-acl --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=network-acl,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-isolated-nacl}]" --query NetworkAcl.NetworkAclId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id $NACL_ID --ingress --rule-number 100 --protocol -1 --cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --rule-action allow --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id $NACL_ID --egress --rule-number 100 --protocol -1 --cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --rule-action allow --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - NACL associations
cliBlocks.content:
$A1 = aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=$ISOLATED_A_ID --query "NetworkAcls[0].Associations[0].NetworkAclAssociationId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-association --association-id $A1 --network-acl-id $NACL_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$A2 = aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=$ISOLATED_B_ID --query "NetworkAcls[0].Associations[0].NetworkAclAssociationId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-association --association-id $A2 --network-acl-id $NACL_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: Endpoint SG accepts 443 only from client SG.
Isolated NACL permits VPC-local traffic both directions and denies other traffic.

verificationChecks.text: Both isolated subnets use the custom NACL.
The learner can state SG=stateful, NACL=stateless.

tasks.title: Create the Flow Logs bucket and S3 gateway endpoint
tasks.goal: Create a private S3 bucket and associate an S3 gateway endpoint with private and isolated route tables.
tasks.whyItMatters: Gateway endpoints are route-table based and do not create endpoint ENIs.
tasks.examRelevance: Gateway endpoints are the low-cost private path for supported services such as S3/DynamoDB.

browserSteps.instruction: Open S3 and create fa-vpc-flow-<account-id> in eu-west-2 with Block Public Access enabled.
Open VPC > Endpoints > Create endpoint.
Name: fa-vpc-s3-gateway-endpoint.
Service: com.amazonaws.eu-west-2.s3, Type Gateway.
VPC: fa-vpc-core.
Select fa-vpc-private-a-rt, fa-vpc-private-b-rt, fa-vpc-isolated-a-rt and fa-vpc-isolated-b-rt.
Use a custom endpoint policy limited to the training flow-log bucket; the CLI route replaces FLOW_LOG_BUCKET_ARN with the exact derived ARN.
Create the endpoint and wait for Available.
Inspect the four route tables and identify the S3 managed-prefix-list route.
Confirm no endpoint ENI/security group exists for the gateway endpoint.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create Flow Logs bucket
cliBlocks.content:
$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID = aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-vpc-admin --query Account --output text
$FLOW_BUCKET = "fa-vpc-flow-$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID"
aws s3api create-bucket --bucket $FLOW_BUCKET --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - build endpoint policy
cliBlocks.content:
$POLICY = (Get-Content .\s3-endpoint-policy-template.json -Raw).Replace("FLOW_LOG_BUCKET_ARN","arn:aws:s3:::$FLOW_BUCKET")
$POLICY | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 .\s3-endpoint-policy.json

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create gateway endpoint
cliBlocks.content: $S3_ENDPOINT_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --service-name com.amazonaws.eu-west-2.s3 --vpc-endpoint-type Gateway --route-table-ids $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID $ISOLATED_A_RT_ID $ISOLATED_B_RT_ID --policy-document file://s3-endpoint-policy.json --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc-endpoint,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-s3-gateway-endpoint}]" --query VpcEndpoint.VpcEndpointId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect endpoint
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $S3_ENDPOINT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: S3 gateway endpoint is Available.
Selected RTs contain S3 prefix-list routes.
The S3 bucket remains private.

verificationChecks.text: No endpoint ENI exists.
Policy scope is limited to the flow-log bucket.

tasks.title: Create an SSM interface endpoint in isolated subnets
tasks.goal: Create an interface VPC endpoint with private DNS and one ENI in each isolated subnet.
tasks.whyItMatters: Interface endpoints use PrivateLink, subnet ENIs and security groups instead of gateway routes.
tasks.examRelevance: Use interface endpoints when isolated/private workloads need supported AWS APIs without internet/NAT.
warnings: Interface endpoints incur hourly/data-processing charges until deleted.

browserSteps.instruction: Open VPC > Endpoints > Create endpoint.
Name: fa-vpc-ssm-interface-endpoint.
Service: com.amazonaws.eu-west-2.ssm.
VPC: fa-vpc-core.
Enable private DNS.
Select fa-vpc-isolated-a and fa-vpc-isolated-b.
Security group: fa-vpc-endpoint-sg.
Create and wait for Available.
Inspect Subnets and Network interfaces; confirm one endpoint ENI per selected subnet.
Compare with the S3 gateway endpoint: interface endpoint has ENIs/SG/private DNS; gateway endpoint has route-table entries.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create SSM endpoint
cliBlocks.content: $SSM_ENDPOINT_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --service-name com.amazonaws.eu-west-2.ssm --subnet-ids $ISOLATED_A_ID $ISOLATED_B_ID --security-group-ids $ENDPOINT_SG_ID --private-dns-enabled --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc-endpoint,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-ssm-interface-endpoint}]" --query VpcEndpoint.VpcEndpointId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect endpoint
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $SSM_ENDPOINT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: SSM endpoint reaches Available.
It has ENIs in isolated-a and isolated-b.
PrivateDnsEnabled is true.

verificationChecks.text: Endpoint uses fa-vpc-endpoint-sg.
Isolated RTs still have no default internet route.

tasks.title: Create fa-vpc-peer and connect it with VPC peering
tasks.goal: Create a second non-overlapping VPC and explicit bidirectional private routes through a peering connection.
tasks.whyItMatters: Peering is direct one-to-one connectivity and is not transitive.
tasks.examRelevance: Peering fits simple VPC pairs; TGW fits larger hub-and-spoke designs.

browserSteps.instruction: Create VPC fa-vpc-peer with CIDR 10.90.0.0/16.
Create fa-vpc-peer-a 10.90.10.0/24 in eu-west-2a and fa-vpc-peer-b 10.90.11.0/24 in eu-west-2b.
Create fa-vpc-peer-rt and associate both peer subnets.
Create peering connection fa-vpc-peering from fa-vpc-core to fa-vpc-peer.
Accept the same-account request.
Add 10.90.0.0/16 -> fa-vpc-peering to fa-vpc-private-a-rt and fa-vpc-private-b-rt.
Add 10.80.0.0/16 -> fa-vpc-peering to fa-vpc-peer-rt.
Do not add peer routes to isolated route tables.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create peer VPC/subnets
cliBlocks.content:
$PEER_VPC_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-peer}]" --query Vpc.VpcId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PEER_A_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $PEER_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.90.10.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-peer-a}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PEER_B_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $PEER_VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.90.11.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-peer-b}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - peer RT
cliBlocks.content:
$PEER_RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $PEER_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-peer-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --subnet-id $PEER_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --subnet-id $PEER_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - peering and routes
cliBlocks.content:
$PCX_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --peer-vpc-id $PEER_VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc-peering-connection,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-peering}]" --query VpcPeeringConnection.VpcPeeringConnectionId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id $PCX_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id $PCX_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id $PCX_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id $PCX_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: Peering status is Active.
Private core RTs route 10.90.0.0/16 via peering.
Peer RT returns 10.80.0.0/16 via peering.

verificationChecks.text: Isolated RTs have no peering route.
Learner can explain non-transitive peering.

tasks.title: Replace peering with Transit Gateway routing
tasks.goal: Remove peering routes/connection, create fa-vpc-tgw, attach both VPCs and route private tiers through it.
tasks.whyItMatters: The transition demonstrates mesh versus hub-and-spoke routing.
tasks.examRelevance: TGW scales connectivity across many VPC/VPN attachments and route tables.
warnings: Transit Gateway and VPC attachments incur hourly charges until cleanup.

browserSteps.instruction: Delete the peering routes from both core private RTs and fa-vpc-peer-rt.
Delete fa-vpc-peering.
Create Transit Gateway fa-vpc-tgw with default association and propagation enabled.
Wait for Available.
Create attachment fa-vpc-tgw-core-attachment using fa-vpc-private-a and fa-vpc-private-b.
Create attachment fa-vpc-tgw-peer-attachment using fa-vpc-peer-a and fa-vpc-peer-b.
Wait for both attachments Available.
Inspect the default TGW route table and confirm both VPC CIDRs are propagated.
Add 10.90.0.0/16 -> fa-vpc-tgw to both core private RTs.
Add 10.80.0.0/16 -> fa-vpc-tgw to fa-vpc-peer-rt.
Do not add TGW routes to isolated RTs.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - remove peering path
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id $PCX_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create TGW
cliBlocks.content: $TGW_ID = aws ec2 create-transit-gateway --description "fa-vpc training transit gateway" --tag-specifications "ResourceType=transit-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-tgw}]" --query TransitGateway.TransitGatewayId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait TGW
cliBlocks.content: do { Start-Sleep 10; $S = aws ec2 describe-transit-gateways --transit-gateway-ids $TGW_ID --query "TransitGateways[0].State" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin } until ($S -eq "available")

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create attachments
cliBlocks.content:
$CORE_TGW_ATTACH_ID = aws ec2 create-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-id $TGW_ID --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --subnet-ids $PRIVATE_A_ID $PRIVATE_B_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=transit-gateway-attachment,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-tgw-core-attachment}]" --query TransitGatewayVpcAttachment.TransitGatewayAttachmentId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$PEER_TGW_ATTACH_ID = aws ec2 create-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-id $TGW_ID --vpc-id $PEER_VPC_ID --subnet-ids $PEER_A_ID $PEER_B_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=transit-gateway-attachment,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-tgw-peer-attachment}]" --query TransitGatewayVpcAttachment.TransitGatewayAttachmentId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - add TGW routes
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --transit-gateway-id $TGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --transit-gateway-id $TGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --transit-gateway-id $TGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: Peering path is removed.
TGW and both attachments become Available.
VPC RTs use TGW for remote VPC CIDRs.

verificationChecks.text: TGW route table propagates both CIDRs.
Isolated RTs remain outside the TGW path.

tasks.title: Complete the PrivateLink provider/consumer plan
tasks.goal: Define service-level private access from fa-vpc-core to a service in fa-vpc-peer without routed whole-VPC connectivity.
tasks.whyItMatters: PrivateLink narrows connectivity to a service boundary instead of exchanging VPC CIDR routes.
tasks.examRelevance: Choose PrivateLink when consumers should reach a service, not the provider network.

browserSteps.instruction: Open privatelink-plan.json.
Review provider sequence: private targets -> internal NLB -> endpoint service -> allowed principals.
Review consumer sequence: interface endpoint in private subnets -> endpoint SG -> private DNS when appropriate.
Open VPC > Endpoint services > Create endpoint service and inspect the current NLB requirement.
Do not create the NLB or custom endpoint service in this lab.
Open VPC > Endpoints and inspect Other endpoint services for consumer connections.
Close the wizard without creating resources.
State the distinction: PrivateLink is service-level private access; peering/TGW are routed network connectivity.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect plan
cliBlocks.content: Get-Content .\privatelink-plan.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json | Format-List

editableBlocks.title: privatelink-plan.json
editableBlocks.content:
{
  "pattern": "AWS PrivateLink endpoint service",
  "providerVpc": "fa-vpc-peer",
  "consumerVpc": "fa-vpc-core",
  "providerSequence": [
    "Deploy private service targets",
    "Create internal NLB fa-vpc-privatelink-nlb",
    "Create endpoint service fa-vpc-privatelink-service",

    "Keep acceptance required when explicit approval is wanted"
  ],
  "consumerSequence": [
    "Create interface endpoint in fa-vpc-private-a and fa-vpc-private-b",

  ]
}

expectedResults: PrivateLink provider/consumer sequence is complete.
No NLB/custom endpoint-service charge is created.

verificationChecks.text: Learner can explain PrivateLink versus peering/TGW.

tasks.title: Complete the Site-to-Site VPN architecture plan
tasks.goal: Plan both VGW and TGW VPN patterns using two IPsec tunnels and BGP-capable routing.
tasks.whyItMatters: A software-only lab cannot establish a real tunnel without a customer gateway device.
tasks.examRelevance: VPN is the encrypted internet-based hybrid path; TGW is the scalable AWS routing hub option.

browserSteps.instruction: Open hybrid-connectivity-plan.json.
Review on-premises CIDR 192.168.100.0/24, documentation-only public IP 198.51.100.10 and ASN 65010.
Review single-VPC path: customer gateway -> two tunnels -> VGW -> VPC routes.
Review multi-VPC path: customer gateway -> two tunnels -> TGW VPN attachment -> TGW/VPC routes.
Open VPC > Customer gateways and inspect IP/ASN fields.
Open Site-to-Site VPN connections and inspect target gateway choices.
Do not create a billed VPN connection because no real customer device exists.
Confirm AWS provides two tunnels and the customer device must use the downloaded configuration.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect VPN plan
cliBlocks.content: (Get-Content .\hybrid-connectivity-plan.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).siteToSiteVpn | Format-List

editableBlocks.title: hybrid-connectivity-plan.json

expectedResults: VPN plan contains VGW and TGW patterns.
No billed VPN connection is created.

verificationChecks.text: Learner can explain customer gateway versus AWS-side gateway.
Plan contains two tunnels.

tasks.title: Complete the Direct Connect architecture plan
tasks.goal: Plan private-VIF/VGW and transit-VIF/TGW Direct Connect patterns.
tasks.whyItMatters: Direct Connect depends on physical/partner connectivity; architecture selection is the meaningful disposable-lab outcome.
tasks.examRelevance: Use private VIF for private VPC access and transit VIF with DX gateway/TGW for scalable multi-VPC connectivity.

browserSteps.instruction: Open hybrid-connectivity-plan.json.
Review small-VPC path: connection -> private VIF -> DX gateway -> VGW -> VPC.
Review multi-VPC path: connection -> transit VIF -> DX gateway -> TGW -> VPC attachments.
Open Direct Connect console and inspect Connections and Virtual interfaces.
Do not order/create a connection.
Confirm BGP is used to exchange prefixes.
Record resilience: remove single connection/location dependencies and consider VPN backup.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect DX plan
cliBlocks.content: (Get-Content .\hybrid-connectivity-plan.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).directConnect | Format-List

expectedResults: Direct Connect plan distinguishes private VIF and transit VIF patterns.
No physical/partner connection is ordered.

verificationChecks.text: Learner can explain DX gateway and transit VIF roles.

tasks.title: Enable VPC Flow Logs to the private S3 bucket
tasks.goal: Create an ALL-traffic VPC Flow Log targeting the private account-derived S3 bucket.
tasks.whyItMatters: Flow Logs provide IP-flow metadata for routing/SG/NACL troubleshooting.
tasks.examRelevance: ACCEPT/REJECT records are a common evidence source for network troubleshooting.

browserSteps.instruction: Open VPC > Your VPCs > fa-vpc-core > Flow logs.
Choose Create flow log.
Name: fa-vpc-flow-log.
Filter: All.
Aggregation interval: 10 minutes.
Destination: S3.
Bucket ARN: arn:aws:s3:::fa-vpc-flow-<account-id>.
Create and wait for Active.
Open the S3 bucket and inspect its delivery prefix/policy.
Log files can take several minutes and require traffic; Active status is the required immediate success condition.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create Flow Log
cliBlocks.content:
$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID = aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-vpc-admin --query Account --output text
$FLOW_BUCKET = "fa-vpc-flow-$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID"
$FLOW_LOG_ID = aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids $CORE_VPC_ID --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type s3 --log-destination "arn:aws:s3:::$FLOW_BUCKET" --max-aggregation-interval 600 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc-flow-log,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-vpc-flow-log}]" --query FlowLogIds[0] --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect Flow Log
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-flow-logs --flow-log-ids $FLOW_LOG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect S3
cliBlocks.content: aws s3 ls "s3://$FLOW_BUCKET/" --recursive --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: Flow Log is Active and captures ALL traffic.
Destination is the private training bucket.

verificationChecks.text: Flow Log references fa-vpc-core.
Learner can explain ACCEPT/REJECT metadata versus packet payload.

tasks.title: Review SAA-C03 VPC and hybrid-networking decisions
tasks.goal: Consolidate subnet routing, SG/NACL, endpoints, peering, TGW, PrivateLink, VPN, Direct Connect and Flow Logs.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam is about selecting the correct connectivity boundary and routing model.
tasks.examRelevance: Each networking service solves a different scope: subnet, ENI, service, VPC mesh/hub or hybrid edge.

browserSteps.instruction: Public subnet: route to IGW plus suitable resource addressing/security.
Private subnet: no direct inbound internet; this lab uses NAT for outbound IPv4.
Isolated subnet: no default internet/NAT route; explicit endpoints/private routes can still exist.
SG: stateful ENI allow rules.
NACL: stateless subnet allow/deny rules.
NAT gateway: private IPv4 egress, not transitive peering.
Gateway endpoint: route-table path for supported services such as S3/DynamoDB.
Interface endpoint: PrivateLink ENIs, SGs and private DNS.
Peering: direct one-to-one, non-transitive.
Transit Gateway: hub-and-spoke many-VPC/VPN routing.
PrivateLink: private access to a service without broad provider-VPC routing.
Site-to-Site VPN: two IPsec tunnels to a customer gateway device.
Direct Connect: physical/partner connectivity using private/transit VIFs and a DX gateway.
Flow Logs: network-flow metadata for ACCEPT/REJECT evidence.
Current AWS also offers Regional NAT gateways; this lab deliberately uses a zonal public NAT to keep classic subnet-route/AZ trade-offs visible.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - route summary
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$CORE_VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - endpoint summary
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$CORE_VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - TGW attachments
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-vpc-attachments --filters Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=$TGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

expectedResults: Learner can distinguish subnet class from filtering controls.
Learner can select the correct endpoint/inter-VPC/hybrid option from a requirement.

verificationChecks.text: Core private RTs contain NAT default route plus TGW route to 10.90.0.0/16.
Isolated RTs contain no default internet route.

tasks.title: Delete endpoints, TGW, NAT and VPC resources
tasks.goal: Delete every active cloud resource in reverse dependency order before removing credentials.
tasks.whyItMatters: Network ENIs/attachments/routes block VPC deletion if removed out of order.
tasks.examRelevance: Safe teardown follows the same dependency graph as design.
warnings: Use console or describe commands to rebuild exact fa-vpc IDs before any omitted repetitive route-table/subnet delete command; never broaden deletion to unrelated resources.

browserSteps.instruction: Delete fa-vpc-flow-log.
Delete fa-vpc-ssm-interface-endpoint and wait for endpoint ENIs to disappear.
Delete fa-vpc-s3-gateway-endpoint.
Delete TGW routes from both core private RTs and fa-vpc-peer-rt.
Delete both TGW VPC attachments and wait for deletion.
Delete fa-vpc-tgw.
Disassociate and delete fa-vpc-peer-rt; delete peer-a, peer-b and fa-vpc-peer.
Delete fa-vpc-nat-a, wait for Deleted, then release fa-vpc-nat-eip.
Delete fa-vpc-endpoint-sg then fa-vpc-client-sg.
Move both isolated subnets back to the default NACL, then delete fa-vpc-isolated-nacl.
Disassociate/delete all five custom core route tables.
Detach/delete fa-vpc-igw.
Delete all six core subnets, then fa-vpc-core.
Empty/delete fa-vpc-flow-<account-id>.
Verify no NAT, interface endpoint or TGW remains.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete Flow/endpoints
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-flow-logs --flow-log-ids $FLOW_LOG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $SSM_ENDPOINT_ID $S3_ENDPOINT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - remove TGW routes
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.90.0.0/16 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete TGW attachments/TGW
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-attachment-id $CORE_TGW_ATTACH_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-attachment-id $PEER_TGW_ATTACH_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete NAT/EIP
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id $NAT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
do { Start-Sleep 10; $N = aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --nat-gateway-ids $NAT_ID --query "NatGateways[0].State" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin } until ($N -eq "deleted")
aws ec2 release-address --allocation-id $EIP_ALLOC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - empty/delete Flow bucket
cliBlocks.content:
aws s3 rm "s3://$FLOW_BUCKET" --recursive --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws s3api delete-bucket --bucket $FLOW_BUCKET --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for endpoint deletion
cliBlocks.content: do { Start-Sleep 10; $E = aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $SSM_ENDPOINT_ID --query "VpcEndpoints[0].State" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin 2>$null } until (-not $E -or $E -eq "deleted")

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait/delete TGW
cliBlocks.content:
do { Start-Sleep 10; $LEFT = aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-vpc-attachments --filters Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=$TGW_ID --query "TransitGatewayVpcAttachments[?State!='deleted']" --output json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin } until ($LEFT -eq "[]")
aws ec2 delete-transit-gateway --transit-gateway-id $TGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild peer RT associations
cliBlocks.content: $PEER_ASSOCS = aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids $PEER_RT_ID --query "RouteTables[0].Associations[?Main==`false`].RouteTableAssociationId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - disassociate peer RT
cliBlocks.content: foreach ($ID in ($PEER_ASSOCS -split "\s+")) { if ($ID) { aws ec2 disassociate-route-table --association-id $ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin } }

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete peer RT/subnets/VPC
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-route-table --route-table-id $PEER_RT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $PEER_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $PEER_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-vpc --vpc-id $PEER_VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete SGs
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id $ENDPOINT_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id $CLIENT_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - restore isolated A default NACL
cliBlocks.content:
$DEFAULT_NACL_ID = aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$CORE_VPC_ID Name=default,Values=true --query "NetworkAcls[0].NetworkAclId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
$ISO_A_ASSOC = aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids $NACL_ID --query "NetworkAcls[0].Associations[?SubnetId=='$ISOLATED_A_ID'].NetworkAclAssociationId | [0]" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-association --association-id $ISO_A_ASSOC --network-acl-id $DEFAULT_NACL_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - restore isolated B default NACL
cliBlocks.content:
$ISO_B_ASSOC = aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids $NACL_ID --query "NetworkAcls[0].Associations[?SubnetId=='$ISOLATED_B_ID'].NetworkAclAssociationId | [0]" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-association --association-id $ISO_B_ASSOC --network-acl-id $DEFAULT_NACL_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-network-acl --network-acl-id $NACL_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - disassociate/delete public RT
PowerShell - disassociate/delete private A RT
cliBlocks.content:
$ID = aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --query "RouteTables[0].Associations[?Main==`false`].RouteTableAssociationId | [0]" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 disassociate-route-table --association-id $ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-route-table --route-table-id $PRIVATE_A_RT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - disassociate/delete private B RT
cliBlocks.content:
$ID = aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --query "RouteTables[0].Associations[?Main==`false`].RouteTableAssociationId | [0]" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 disassociate-route-table --association-id $ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-route-table --route-table-id $PRIVATE_B_RT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - detach/delete IGW
cliBlocks.content:

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete six core subnets
cliBlocks.content:
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $PUBLIC_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $PUBLIC_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $PRIVATE_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $PRIVATE_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete core VPC
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 delete-vpc --vpc-id $CORE_VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-vpc-admin

Cloud cleanup finishes before IAM cleanup.

tasks.title: Delete the temporary IAM identity and local files

browserSteps.instruction: Confirm Task 17 has removed every fa-vpc cloud resource.
Sign in as root only now.
Delete fa-vpc-admin's access key.
Detach and delete fa-vpc-admin-policy.
Delete fa-vpc-admin and sign out of root.
Remove only the fa-vpc-admin AWS CLI profile.
Delete C:\aws-labs\fa-vpc last.
Affirm the programme cleanup acknowledgement.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - clear profile
cliBlocks.content:
aws configure set aws_access_key_id "" --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws configure set aws_secret_access_key "" --profile fa-vpc-admin
aws configure set region "" --profile fa-vpc-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete local folder
cliBlocks.content:
Set-Location C:\
Remove-Item "C:\aws-labs\fa-vpc" -Recurse -Force

expectedResults: Temporary IAM user/access key/policy/profile are removed.
Local folder is deleted last.

verificationChecks.text: Unrelated identities/profiles are unchanged.
No fa-vpc local file remains.

troubleshooting.title: Private subnet has no NAT default route
troubleshooting.likelyCause: NAT not Available or route added to wrong table.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify fa-vpc-nat-a is Available and 0.0.0.0/0 exists in both private route tables.

troubleshooting.title: Isolated subnet unexpectedly has internet route
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Wrong RT association or default route was added.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify isolated subnet associations and remove any 0.0.0.0/0 from isolated route tables.

troubleshooting.title: SSM interface endpoint remains Pending
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Endpoint ENI/DNS/security configuration is invalid or still provisioning.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm DNS hostnames are enabled, both isolated subnet IDs are correct, and endpoint SG belongs to fa-vpc-core.

troubleshooting.title: S3 gateway endpoint route missing
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Route table was not associated with endpoint.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the endpoint Route tables tab or modify-vpc-endpoint to add the exact private/isolated RT IDs.

troubleshooting.title: Peering stays Pending Acceptance
troubleshooting.fix: Accept fa-vpc-peering and wait for Active before routing.

troubleshooting.title: TGW attachment is Available but VPC path is incomplete
troubleshooting.likelyCause: VPC route to TGW is missing even if TGW propagation exists.
troubleshooting.fix: Check both VPC route tables and the TGW default route table propagation.

troubleshooting.title: Security group cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Interface endpoint ENI still uses fa-vpc-endpoint-sg.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete the interface endpoint and wait for ENI removal before deleting SG.

troubleshooting.title: VPC cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Endpoint, NAT, TGW attachment, subnet, custom RT or IGW remains.
troubleshooting.fix: Follow reverse-dependency cleanup; do not broaden deletion.

troubleshooting.title: Flow Log bucket has no files yet
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Delivery is asynchronous or little traffic occurred.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify Flow Log status Active and correct S3 destination; wait several minutes.

programmeCleanup.action: Delete interface endpoint and wait for ENIs.
Delete peer RT associations/RT, peer subnets and peer VPC.
Delete NAT, wait, then release EIP.
Delete both SGs after endpoint is gone.
Restore default NACL associations, then delete custom NACL.
Remove explicit associations and delete RTs.
Use root only after cloud verification to remove identity.

programmeCleanupAcknowledgement: I verified that fa-vpc-flow-log, fa-vpc-ssm-interface-endpoint and fa-vpc-s3-gateway-endpoint are deleted; all routes to fa-vpc-tgw, both Transit Gateway VPC attachments and fa-vpc-tgw are deleted; the earlier fa-vpc-peering connection was removed before Transit Gateway routing was introduced; fa-vpc-peer and its route table/subnets are deleted; fa-vpc-nat-a and fa-vpc-nat-eip are deleted; fa-vpc-endpoint-sg, fa-vpc-client-sg and fa-vpc-isolated-nacl are deleted; all five custom core route tables, fa-vpc-igw, all six core subnets and fa-vpc-core are deleted; the fa-vpc-flow-<account-id> bucket is empty and deleted; no custom PrivateLink service, Site-to-Site VPN connection or Direct Connect connection was created; the temporary fa-vpc-admin access key, fa-vpc-admin-policy, IAM user and CLI profile are removed; unrelated resources and profiles are unchanged; and only then was C:\aws-labs\fa-vpc deleted.

warnings.cost: This lab creates a public NAT gateway, Elastic IP, an SSM interface endpoint, a Transit Gateway with two VPC attachments and S3/Flow Logs storage. These can incur charges. PrivateLink custom service, Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect remain architecture-only specifically to avoid unnecessary NLB, VPN and physical-connectivity cost.
warnings.safety: Delete only exact fa-vpc resources and generated IDs rebuilt from those names. Never force VPC deletion or delete unrelated default/main resources.
warnings.credentials: Never create root access keys and never put fa-vpc-admin access-key values in architecture files, screenshots, chat or Study Tracker. Enter them only through protected aws configure prompts.
warnings.region: Every hands-on cloud resource is created in eu-west-2. Core and peer subnet pairs use eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.
